learning_outcomes.text: Communicate knowledge and conclusions, both orally and in writing, to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Possess learning skills that allow continuous study throughout life for adequate professional development.
Incorporate ICT and Industrial Engineering technologies and tools into their professional activities.
Know and apply knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to the practice of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge about the fundamentals of automation and control methods.
Knowledge about the fundamentals of automation and control methods.

syllabus_topics: Types and classification of sensors and actuators
Boolean Algebra. Combinational systems and their representation (KOP, FUP)
Mealy and Moore state machines. Representation systems: state diagrams, transition tables
Activation and retention equations. Programming using contacts (KOP)
Introduction to Grafcet modeling and basic programming
Programming using activation-retention / latching coils in instruction list language
Programming logical operations in the PLC (STEP 7)
Practical cases: implementation of the Grafcet model

assessment_methods.method: Second written exam (Ordinary Call Theory Test)

assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, practices are a compulsory pass/fail block without weight on the final grade; a minimum of 3 on the second written test is required. The final grade is the better of (40% first test + 60% second test) or (100% second test). For the extraordinary call, passing the practice block and scoring above 5 on a 100% weighted written test are required. If the practice block is not passed, the final grade will be the minimum between the written test score and 4.
